newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SAMPRAS STRETCHES UNBEATEN RUN TO 21 MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS STRETCHES UNBEATEN RUN TO 21 MATCHES.

text.p: Pete Sampras stretched his unbeaten run to 21 matches with a comfortable 6-3 6-4 victory over unseeded Dutchman Jan Siemerink in the Stuttgart Open semifinals on Saturday.

The triple Wimbledon champion, who has won his last three tournaments including the U.S. Open and is unbeaten indoors this year, took 79 minutes to clinch his place in Sunday's final of the $2.2 million indoor event.
The winning streak is the second longest of his career. In 1994 the 25-year-old American won 29 consecutive matches.
Sampras's serve-and-volley game is perfectly suited to the swift indoor courts, although the Stuttgart surface is not one of the fastest on the circuit.
The American made a key break of serve in the sixth game to lead 4-2 before taking the first set in 32 minutes.
Although the world number one dropped his serve at the start of the second set, he soon bounced back with breaks in the third and seventh games on his way to a largely easy victory.
